videos.script: Okay so everyone asks me about Varanasi, and I always say the same thing. First, do NOT go in May — it is way too unbearable humidity and heat. The best time? November, hands down. And when you are there, skip the tourist restaurants. Go where the locals eat. Ask any rickshaw driver for the best kachori sabzi from the ghats. NakshIQ scores Varanasi a 4.4 out of 5 right now. Check it before you book. Link in bio.

I just did the Hampta Pass trek and my legs are still shaking, but oh my god, worth it. The altitude at Hampta Pass is no joke — 4,270m at the pass and your body feels every metre. You need at least 2 days to acclimatize. Do not rush it. Carry crampons, trekking poles, and a zero-degree sleeping bag — the weather changes in minutes up there. NakshIQ rates the trek difficulty at 4.1 out of 5. Check the full breakdown before you pack. Link in bio.

There is a reason people keep coming back to Rishikesh, and it is not just the views. The energy in Rishikesh is different. You feel it the moment you arrive. Whether it is the a ten-day silent Vipassana retreat or just the silence, it does something to you. Best time to go: March, when it is quiet and the weather is perfect. NakshIQ gives it a 4.5. Check the wellness guide. Link in bio.

I had absolutely no idea Hampi existed until a friend told me, and now it is my favourite place in India. A friend told me about Hampi and I thought — really? But then I saw the sunrise over the boulder landscape with ancient temples everywhere and it was one of the best experiences I have had in India. NakshIQ gives it a 4.2 for November. Absolute hidden gem. Link in bio.

I did not know what Ayurveda actually was until I experienced it in Dharamsala. I did not really understand Tibetan meditation at a monastery near McLeod Ganj until I experienced it in Dharamsala. The way they teach it there, with such patience and tradition — it is humbling. If you are thinking about going, October is the sweet spot. NakshIQ scores it a 4.3 for that month. Link in bio.

They said Valley of Flowers was tough. They were not kidding. But here is why you should still do it. The views at Valley of Flowers are unreal, but the fourteen-kilometre trek through monsoon mud and river crossings caught me off guard. My advice? book ahead. And download the NakshIQ offline map before you go — there is zero signal up there. They score the conditions at 4.0 right now. Link in bio.

Okay so here is what I wish someone had told me before my first trip to Goa. Here is the stuff the travel blogs do not tell you about Goa. South Goa for peace, North Goa for parties — do not mix them up. Also, beach shacks in Agonda are half the price of Palolem. I check NakshIQ for every trip now — they score everything from safety to weather. Goa is at a 3.8 for November. Link in bio.
